root_cause.text: An off-by-one bug in the liquidio VF driver's setup_nic_devices() error-cleanup path used `while (i--)`, which skipped freeing the current failed NIC device index and leaked its allocated resources.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states that on failure the code jumps to `setup_nic_dev_free` and "`while(i--)` skip[s] the failing index `i`, causing a memory leak," and the patch changes the cleanup from `while (i--)` to `do { ... liquidio_destroy_nic_device(octeon_dev, i); } while (i--);` so the current index is also cleaned up.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix NIC setup failure cleanup to always destroy the current interface before decrementing the index.
intent_record.what: The cleanup loop in setup_nic_devices() was changed from a pre-decrement-style `while (i--) { ... }` loop to a post-action `do { ... } while (i--);` loop, leaving the loop body unchanged.
intent_record.how: This makes the cleanup block execute at least once when control reaches the failure path, ensuring the NIC device at the current index `i` is reported and destroyed before decrementing. It prevents skipping cleanup of the first or current failed interface due to the original loop condition evaluating false before entering the loop.

grouping_result.intent: Fix NIC setup failure cleanup to always destroy the current interface before decrementing the index.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly fixes the setup_nic_devices() error-cleanup off-by-one behavior by ensuring the current failed NIC device is destroyed before decrementing the index, which matches the described leak root cause.

candidates.rationale: This post-decrement loop condition is the direct off-by-one root cause: it decrements i before entering the body for cleanup, so the currently failed NIC device index is skipped and its resources are not destroyed.

vuln_statements.explanation: This post-decrement loop condition causes an off-by-one error in the error-cleanup path: cleanup starts only after decrementing i, so the currently failed NIC device index is skipped and its allocated resources are leaked.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable cleanup logic is shown directly in `setup_nic_devices()`. On failure, control reaches `setup_nic_dev_fail:` / `setup_nic_wait_intr:` and then runs `while (i--) { ... liquidio_destroy_nic_device(octeon_dev, i); }`. This is the off-by-one pattern described in the root cause. Because `i--` is evaluated as the loop condition, when failure happens at the current index `i`, the first condition check uses the old value and then decrements `i` before entering the body, so the body starts with `i - 1`. That skips cleanup of the currently failed NIC device index. The function allocates and stores per-interface resources before later operations may fail, e.g. `netdev = alloc_etherdev_mq(...)`, then `props = &octeon_dev->props[i]; props->gmxport = ...; props->netdev = netdev;`, and later `register_netdev(netdev)` may fail and jump to cleanup. In that case, the current `props[i].netdev` is set, but the `while (i--)` cleanup will only destroy lower indices and leak the current one. There is no corrected cleanup such as including the current index explicitly or using a different loop form, so the fix is not present.
